name: Summit Valley Lookout Site
summary: Former Six Rivers NF tower site in Del Norte County; construction and removal dates unknown; a June 2020 hiker found only rocks, metal and chimney pieces.
design: Short, open timber tower with a partial catwalk; FFLOS says it appears to follow a USFS R1 cabin plan
status_note: Former lookout site; in June 2020 a hiker found only a square of loose rocks strewn with metal and flattened chimney pieces; no source describes a standing tower
agency: US Forest Service - Six Rivers National Forest

access.note: Trailhead on FS 15 (G-O Road) and the trail lies in the Smith River National Recreation Area; the 2020 summit route was faint and no source says whether it is maintained or open

visit.trail_note: Summit Valley Trail: South Fork Road from Hwy 199 (about 13.7 miles), then FS 15 (G-O Road) about 15 miles to the trailhead; 1.5 miles one way to the valley meadow; rated moderate, downhill; the 2020 route to the summit used cairns and was hard to follow near the top

events.note: May 1940 Siskiyou National Forest guard placement plan: view largely duplicates Buck Mountain; chief value is fire suppression; lightning the sole cause of fires
Coast and Geodetic Survey station description calls it a U.S. Forest Service lookout tower on the top of Summit Valley
Registered January 28, 2020 as US 1891, CA 86; nominated by Brad Eells
June 2020 hiker found a square of loose rocks strewn with metal marking the former site, with flattened chimney pieces nearby
